# Engine noise diagnosis

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Pour Sea Foam into the gas tank and add it to the oil crankcase. [t659]

[Partial] Pour and spray Sea Foam into the oil crankcase and through the vacuum line. [t659]

[Partial] Pour and add Sea Foam into the first and second gas tanks respectively. [t659]

[Partial] Spray Sea Foam through the throttle body with the engine running. [t659]

## Specifications

- **Sea Foam distribution ratio**: DISPUTED, sources disagree: 1/3 for gas, 1/3 for oil, 1/3 for vacuum line [t659]; 1/2 in crankcase, 1/2 in vacuum line [t659]; 1/2 in each of two tanks [t659]

## Tips & gotchas

- Pour into the vacuum line very slowly to avoid hydrolocking the engine. [t659]
- [Partial] Use this method to clean the intake, ensuring coverage of both sides of the valve and intake since vacuum line spraying covers mainly the left side. [t659]
- Be careful as the computer may not like a reading from the MAF sensor when spraying through the throttle body. [t659]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Forgetting that the engine needs to be running for optimal results, though this risks confusing the MAF sensor. [t659]
